operational-example.copy: Use Audit Event for one traceable event inside an operational surface: who changed what, when it happened, and the resulting status. Use Timeline or an audit table pattern when events become a sequence, filterable history, or investigation flow.

scenario.title: Audit record

items.label: Document verified
items.description: Driver license was approved after review.

rationale: The ZIP timeline reference informs marker size, compact title hierarchy, mono timestamp, and secondary description rhythm.
Flow governs color semantics, density, focus, radius, typography, and state precedence.
One event stays a component; ordered history, filtering, approvals, and investigation belong to patterns.

items.rule: Identifies the event type without replacing text.
Names actor/action/result in a compact readable title and description.
Shows actor, source, or timestamp as supporting context only.
Shows status with text plus semantic tone; never color-only.
Provides local row framing without becoming a timeline container.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, critical, warning, verified, focus, hover, default
items: Keep the event label visible and descriptive.
Do not rely on icon or color alone for status.
Use timestamp text when time is important; do not hide it in title attributes.
Keep focus visible for interactive wrappers owned by a parent pattern.
Escalate to Timeline or Table when the user must compare, filter, or investigate multiple events.

variants.copy: Audit Event has one structural variant. Use tone and state for local event status; do not create business variants such as permission, vehicle, card, or finance inside the component.

states.copy: Audit Event state controls local feedback and status tone. Process state and event ordering stay outside the component.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Structural variant is fixed. The matrix verifies that state and tone remain readable without turning Audit Event into a timeline pattern.

full-width.copy: Audit Event may fill a parent row or panel when the parent owns layout. It should not own list sequencing.

demo.label: Approval needed
demo.description: Policy change is waiting for review.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Density changes spacing, marker size, and title scale. The parent surface decides whether events stack, scroll, or become a timeline/table pattern.

demos.label: Approval needed
demos.description: Policy change is waiting for review.

viewport-organization.copy: Use Audit Event where one event needs context. Use Timeline, Table, or an approval pattern when the viewport needs comparison or workflow.

items.title: Panel
items.rule: Use a single event near the object it explains.

items.title: Dense desktop
items.rule: Use compact density in sidebars or detail panes only when status stays readable.

items.title: Escalate
items.rule: If there is ordering, connectors, filtering, or investigation, use a pattern.

demo.label: Audit sequence
demo.description: More than one event requires Timeline or Table.

playground.copy: Use the playground to verify Audit Event label, tone, state, density, timestamp, and pattern boundary.

api-foundations.copy: Audit Event API exposes one atomic event. Flow owns typography, tone, density, radius, motion, and accessibility; parent patterns own event lists and workflow.

props.name: timestamp
props.notes: Visible time string for the event.

props.name: tone
props.notes: Semantic tone for marker and status badge.

groups.title: Use
items: Use Audit Event for one atomic record.
Translate ZIP timeline details through Flow tokens.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not build a sequence, connector rail, filter, approval flow, or investigation state inside this component.
Do not create business variants for permission, vehicle, card, or finance.
Do not use icon or color as the only status.

groups.title: Review
items: Check dark mode contrast for marker, text, and badge.
Escalate to pattern when more than one event must be compared.

rejectIf: Business-specific variants are added to the component.
A timeline connector or ordered event list is built into Audit Event.
Docs render a non-package audit event instance.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Audit Event as one atomic record. Agents may place it when the job is local; humans confirm whether multiple records require Timeline, Table, or workflow patterns.
canDecide: Use Audit Event for one local record.
Select tone, state, density, timestamp, and status text from the component API.
Keep event meaning readable without color.
mustAsk: The request needs an ordered history, filtering, approval rules, or investigation.
The event status changes business process state.
Accessibility, risk, or reduced-motion expectations are unclear.
rejectIf: The component becomes a timeline, audit table, or workflow.
Required meaning is icon-only, color-only, or motion-only.
A business variant is introduced instead of using tone/state.
miel.handoff: I am using Audit Event as one atomic record. Please confirm whether this remains a single event or should escalate to Timeline/Table/workflow pattern.
